title: The Last Instalment
logline: A family counts out the final payment on gold pawned years ago during a hard season, and walks home carrying back something they had almost stopped expecting to see again.
human_question: Why does being freed from a debt feel different from gaining something new?

premise.story: Over one day, a family makes the last payment on jewellery pawned years earlier during an illness or a bad harvest, receives the item back, and the household adjusts to the debt being gone.
premise.place: A small-town pawn counter and the family's home.
premise.experience: The unglamorous mechanics of debt and repayment, and the quiet, unmarked moment when a long-carried weight is simply not there any more.

concept_links.why: The Margaya grounds its whole argument about release in exactly this: people pawn belongings and sell land to be free of illness or debt, because release is valued above pleasure, and no one would pay that much for something worth nothing [C073-M:L7].

The source distinguishes change that is only temporary relief from change that does not come back; the film can hold that question open about a single family's debt without claiming any larger attainment.

what_camera_could_observe: The counter, the ledger, the final sum counted out in cash
The wrapped item handed back, unwrapped at home
What the family does or does not do differently that evening
Ordinary conversation about the years the debt was carried
what_must_be_real: A real, willing family's real financial history. Nothing about the hardship or the repayment is staged or re-created for the camera.

possible_arc.opening: An ordinary transaction at a pawn counter.
possible_arc.turn: The last note is counted; the item changes hands.
possible_arc.ending_open: The family's own account of what, if anything, feels different now leads the ending.

position_hint: opening candidate: the returned item, or a token connected to the closed debt, could plausibly become Object 10 if the family is willing to part with or duplicate something; a direct, human image of 'something set down.'

requirements: A family willing to be filmed at a real pawn transaction and at home
A pawn business willing to allow filming at the counter

suggestions.name: A market town in the central or hill-country districts
suggestions.region: Central Province (e.g. Matale, Kegalle or Gampola area)
suggestions.why: Small-town pawn counters are common in these market towns.
suggestions.verify: No specific business or family is identified; this is a region-level suggestion only.

risks: Turning a family's hardship into a tidy moral
drop_if: No family will consent to show a real repayment on camera, or would be exposed to embarrassment by it

connections.note: Both ask whether a change is temporary relief or something that does not come back, one through money, one through habit.
A different, non-craft way Object 10 could be acquired at the group's opening.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
